script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Romance
Theme: career transition

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. COFFEE SHOP - MORNING

A young woman, JENNY (mid-20s, dressed professionally), sits at a table, engrossed in her laptop. She takes a sip of her coffee, her gaze fixed on the screen.

Waiter brings over a tray bearing a second cup.

WAITER
(cheerful)
Another one for you, ma'am?

Jenny looks up, startled. She smiles weakly.

JENNY
(softly)
Yes, please.

Waiter sets the cup down and pours the coffee, then nods and leaves. Jenny resumes working, her brow furrowed in concentration.

INT. JENNY'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Jenny enters her apartment, tossing her keys onto a table by the door. She walks through to the living room, the laptop bag slung over her shoulder. The phone rings. She hesitates, then answers it.

JENNY
(into phone)
Hello?

VOICE (off)
(cheerful)
Hey, it's Sam. How's the job search going?

Jenny sighs and sinks into the couch, resting her head in her hand.

JENNY
It's not going well, Sam. I've applied to hundreds of jobs and I've barely gotten any responses. I'm starting to feel like there's something wrong with me.

SAM (off)
(sympathetically)
There's nothing wrong with you, Jenny. The job market is tough right now. Why don't you consider a career change?

Jenny rolls her eyes, a small smile playing at the corners of her lips.

JENNY
(laughing)
A career change? That's easier said than done. I've been a financial analyst for five years. What could I possibly do instead?

Sam is silent for a moment.

SAM (off)
What about...art?

Jenny's eyes widen in surprise.

JENNY
Art? I can't even draw a stick figure!

Sam laughs.

SAM (off)
Well, there's more to art than drawing. What about graphic design? You have a good eye for color and composition. And I know someone who could help you get started.

Jenny's mind races as she considers this new possibility.

INT. DESIGN STUDIO - DAY

Jenny sits at a long table, surrounded by various art supplies and computers. A man in his late 30s, MIKE, looks on approvingly as she fiddles with the software on her laptop.

MIKE
(friendly)
So, you're interested in graphic design? It's a great field. Lots of opportunities.

Jenny nods, looking determined.

JENNY
I'm willing to learn. I just need a chance.

MIKE
Well, I think you have what it takes. Let's get started, shall we?

INT. COFFEE SHOP - AFTERNOON

Jenny sits in the coffee shop, her laptop open in front of her. She's been working for hours, and the sun is starting to set. She looks up as the door opens and Mike enters, carrying a stack of papers.

MIKE
(excited)
Jenny! Look at this!

He sets the papers down in front of her and opens one, revealing a stunning design. Jenny's eyes widen in awe.

JENNY
(whispering)
This is amazing, Mike. How did you do this?

MIKE
(grinning)
Just practice and dedication. And a little bit of talent, of course. But most importantly, you have to believe in yourself.

Jenny nods, a determined look in her eyes.

JENNY
I will. I'm going to do this.

INT. DESIGN STUDIO - EVENING

Jenny works late into the night, fueled by coffee and determination. She struggles with the software, but Mike is always there to offer guidance and encouragement. And slowly, she begins to see progress.

INT. JENNY'S APARTMENT - MORNING

Jenny wakes up early, her mind racing with ideas. She throws on some clothes and rushes to the design studio, her heart pounding with excitement.

INT. DESIGN STUDIO - DAY

Jenny presents her designs to Mike, who studies them intently.

MIKE
(impressed)
Jenny, these are really good. I think you have a natural talent for this.

Jenny beams with pride.

JENNY
Thank you, Mike. I couldn't have done it without you.

MIKE
(smiling)
You did it yourself, Jenny. All I did was give you the opportunity.

Jenny nods, her eyes filled with determination.

JENNY
I'm going to keep going. I'm going to make a career out of this.

MIKE
(encouragingly)
I have no doubt.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - EVENING

Jenny sits at her usual table, her laptop open in front of her. She takes a sip of her coffee, a small smile playing at the corners of her lips. Across the room, she sees Sam entering the coffee shop. He makes his way over to her table, a proud look on his face.

SAM
(excitedly)
Hey, Jenny! Guess what?

Jenny looks up, her eyes shining with curiosity.

JENNY
What? Did you get a new job?

Sam nods, a proud smile on his face.

SAM
Yes, I did. And I want you to be a part of it. They're looking for a graphic designer, and I recommended you.

Jenny's eyes widen in shock and excitement.

JENNY
(shaking her head)
No way. Are you serious?

Sam nods again, a proud grin on his face.

SAM
Absolutely. You're going to ace this interview, Jenny. I have no doubt.

Jenny's eyes fill with tears as she realizes that her career transition might just be within reach.

FADE OUT.
